rationale_code: `git_status` opens the caller-supplied `repo_path` with `git.Repo` and returns `repo.git.status()` output, exposing local working-tree state (file names, untracked paths) from the user's filesystem into the agent context. With no `--repository` restriction any repo path on the host can be read (`val
`git_diff_unstaged` returns `repo.git.diff` output, i.e. the literal contents of uncommitted local file changes, into the agent's context.
`git_diff_staged` returns the staged diff (`--cached`), exposing local file contents from the user's repository.

`git_diff` returns the patch text between the working tree and an arbitrary ref, which is private local repository content (SECRET). The target ref may be a remote-tracking branch or an imported/merged commit from a public upstream, so the returned patch text can contain third-party attacker-authore

`git_commit` calls `repo.index.commit` which only writes a commit object into the local repository; there is no push, network call or externally readable destination, so no SINK. It returns only the commit hash, so no private data is surfaced.

`git_add` stages files; paths are resolved and checked with `relative_to(repo_root)` so staging is confined to the repository working tree, and the tool returns only a fixed success string. No data leaves the host and no code is executed.
`git_reset` calls `repo.index.reset()`, a purely local index mutation returning a constant string; nothing is read out or sent anywhere.

`git_log` returns commit hashes, author names and commit messages from the user's local repository (SECRET). Commit messages and author fields in a repository that tracks a public/third-party upstream are authored by other parties, so the text returned can carry attacker-controlled instructions (UNT
`git_create_branch` only creates a local ref via `repo.create_head` and returns a status string; leading '-' is rejected so no git flag injection. No exfiltration path and no private data returned.

`git_checkout` runs `repo.git.checkout` on a ref validated by `rev_parse` and rejecting leading '-'; it mutates the local working tree but returns only a status string and reaches no external destination. Post-checkout hooks live in the user's own .git directory (not clone-transferred), so no HOSTEX

`git_show` returns the full patch body of an arbitrary revision (`d.diff` decoded) plus author and message, i.e. private local repository file contents (SECRET). Any commit reachable in the repo may originate from a third-party/public upstream, making the returned diff and message text attacker-cont

`git_branch` returns `repo.git.branch` output including local branch names (private repo metadata, SECRET) and, with `branch_type` 'remote'/'all', remote-tracking branch names that are chosen by whoever controls the upstream (UNTRUSTED). `contains`/`not_contains` are guarded against leading '-'.
